title: Like the pearl, Christ is born of the Virgin

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 13, cols. A-B (PDF p. 37)

source_text: Et sicut Margarita ex duabus naturis, ex fulgure nimirum et aqua, occultis quibusdam indiciis ac signis maris provenit: ita quoque Dominus noster Iesus Christus, inconfuse et immutabiliter ex pura ac casta, et impolluta, ac sancta Maria virgine progreditur, in Deitate perfectus, et in humanitate perfectus, Patri per omnia similis, et nobis per omnia consubstantialis, sed omnis peccati expers.
pass_a_gloss: And as the pearl (margarita) from two natures (duae naturae), namely from lightning (fulgur) and water (aqua), by certain hidden indications (occulta indicia) and signs (signa) of the sea (mare) comes forth (provenit): so also our Lord Jesus Christ, without confusion (inconfuse) and unchangeably (immutabiliter) from the pure (pura) and chaste (casta), and undefiled (impolluta), and holy Mary the virgin proceeds (progreditur), in Deity perfect (in Deitate perfectus), and in humanity perfect (in humanitate perfectus), to the Father through all things like (per omnia similis), and to us through all things consubstantial (consubstantialis), but free of all sin (omnis peccati expers).

choices.issue: nobis per omnia consubstantialis, sed omnis peccati expers
choices.choice: 'nobis per omnia consubstantialis, sed omnis peccati expers' echoes Hebrews 4:15 ('tempted in all things as we are, yet without sin'); cited.
'consubstantialis' kept as the exact doctrinal term 'consubstantial'.

choices.issue: occultis quibusdam indiciis ac signis maris provenit
choices.choice: 'occultis quibusdam indiciis ac signis maris provenit' rendered close to the letter ('arising through certain hidden tokens and signs of the sea'; maris goes with signis); the sense is the ancient belief that pearls form from lightning striking the sea.

pass_b_english: And as the pearl comes from two natures, namely lightning and water, arising through certain hidden tokens and signs of the sea, so too our Lord Jesus Christ comes forth, without confusion and without change, from the pure and chaste, undefiled and holy Virgin Mary. He is perfect in Godhead and perfect in manhood, like the Father in all things and consubstantial with us in all things, but without any sin (Hebrews 4:15).
notes: 'nobis per omnia consubstantialis, sed omnis peccati expers' echoes Hebrews 4:15 ('tempted in all things as we are, yet without sin'); cited. The two-natures formula (inconfuse, immutabiliter, perfect in Godhead and manhood, consubstantial with us) is post-Chalcedonian language and supports the later dating noted in the book's description. 'patri per omnia similis' confirmed on the page image (printed p. 13 col. A; lower-case 'patri' as the print writes 'pater' throughout). 'consubstantialis' kept as the exact doctrinal term 'consubstantial'. 'occultis quibusdam indiciis ac signis maris provenit' rendered close to the letter ('arising through certain hidden tokens and signs of the sea'; maris goes with signis); the sense is the ancient belief that pearls form from lightning striking the sea. The margin note on Ephrem's sermon on the pearl is an editor's cross-reference and was not translated.
source_notes: PDF p. 37 = printed p. 13, cols. A-B. Margin: 'Similia ita apud sanctum Ephraem in serm. de Margarita pretiosa, Tomo 3' (editor's cross-reference, not the text).
